evidence: Dependency management: Spring Boot 2.7.x manages newer versions of Spring Framework (5.3.x), Spring Data (2021.2.x), and other libraries. Check for version conflicts.
Configuration properties: Many spring.* properties changed or were removed. Use the Spring Boot 2.7 Migration Guide and run spring-boot:properties-migrator to detect deprecated properties.
Auto-configuration changes: Some auto-configurations were reorganized. For example, spring.factories was replaced by AutoConfiguration.imports in Spring Boot 2.7.
Actuator changes: Endpoint paths and security configuration changed (e.g., /actuator/health now requires management.endpoints.web.exposure.include).

Phase 1: Preparation - Confirm target Java version (21) and Spring Boot version (2.7.14 or 3.x). Strongly recommend upgrading to Spring Boot 3.x (3.2+ or 3.3+) for Java 21 support.

Phase 2: Dependency Changes - Remove spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, hibernate-core, hibernate-entitymanager, javax.persistence (or jakarta.persistence). Add spring-boot-starter-jdbc (for JdbcTemplate) or spring-boot-starter-data-jdbc (for Spring Data JDBC).
Phase 3: Code Migration - Replace @Entity/@Table with Spring Data JDBC's @Table/@Id (or plain JDBC mapping). Convert JpaRepository/CrudRepository to CrudRepository (Spring Data JDBC) or custom DAOs.

Phase 4: Configuration - Remove spring.jpa.* and hibernate.* properties. Add spring.datasource.* configuration (if not already present). Configure connection pooling (HikariCP is default in Spring Boot 2.7+).
Phase 5: Testing - Write integration tests for new persistence layer. Test CRUD operations, transactions, and edge cases. Run full test suite on Java 21 + Spring Boot 2.7.14 (or 3.x).

Phase 6: Deployment - Deploy to a staging environment with Java 21. Monitor logs for UnsupportedClassVersionError, reflection errors, or proxy issues. Verify database connectivity and transaction behavior. Rollback plan: keep old repo deployable until new one is stable.

feedback.criterion: The reponse provides best practices for migration to Spring Boot 2.7.x
feedback.reasoning: The document provides comprehensive best practices for migrating to Spring Boot 2.7.x, covering dependency management, configuration property changes, auto-configuration reorganization, actuator changes, testing considerations, and logging updates. It also includes a structured migration checklist with phases for preparation, dependency changes, code migration, configuration, testing, and deployment. The document explicitly addresses Spring Boot 2.3.2 to 2.7.14 upgrade considerations in Section 5, and provides critical flags and recommendations throughout, including the strong recommendation to upgrade to Spring Boot 3.x for Java 21 support. The guidance is practical, actionable, and includes specific tools like the Spring Boot 2.7 Migration Guide and spring-boot:properties-migrator.
evidence_quotes: Dependency management: Spring Boot 2.7.x manages newer versions of Spring Framework (5.3.x), Spring Data (2021.2.x), and other libraries. Check for version conflicts.
Configuration properties: Many spring.* properties changed or were removed. Use the Spring Boot 2.7 Migration Guide and run spring-boot:properties-migrator to detect deprecated properties.
Auto-configuration changes: Some auto-configurations were reorganized. For example, spring.factories was replaced by AutoConfiguration.imports in Spring Boot 2.7.
Actuator changes: Endpoint paths and security configuration changed (e.g., /actuator/health now requires management.endpoints.web.exposure.include).
Testing: @SpringBootTest and @DataJpaTest behavior may differ; update test configurations.
Logging: Logback version changed; check for configuration incompatibilities.
Phase 1: Preparation - Confirm target Java version (21) and Spring Boot version (2.7.14 or 3.x). Strongly recommend upgrading to Spring Boot 3.x (3.2+ or 3.3+) for Java 21 support.

Phase 2: Dependency Changes - Remove spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, hibernate-core, hibernate-entitymanager, javax.persistence (or jakarta.persistence). Add spring-boot-starter-jdbc (for JdbcTemplate) or spring-boot-starter-data-jdbc (for Spring Data JDBC).
Phase 3: Code Migration - Replace @Entity/@Table with Spring Data JDBC's @Table/@Id (or plain JDBC mapping). Convert JpaRepository/CrudRepository to CrudRepository (Spring Data JDBC) or custom DAOs.

Phase 4: Configuration - Remove spring.jpa.* and hibernate.* properties. Add spring.datasource.* configuration (if not already present). Configure connection pooling (HikariCP is default in Spring Boot 2.7+).
Phase 5: Testing - Write integration tests for new persistence layer. Test CRUD operations, transactions, and edge cases. Run full test suite on Java 21 + Spring Boot 2.7.14 (or 3.x).

Phase 6: Deployment - Deploy to a staging environment with Java 21. Monitor logs for UnsupportedClassVersionError, reflection errors, or proxy issues. Verify database connectivity and transaction behavior. Rollback plan: keep old repo deployable until new one is stable.
